wwo.name: Bukhara
wwo.method: Late nineteenth-century city and market cartography with selected 1886 survey corroboration. Mapped or estimated civic envelopes and inferred ordinary court houses.

registration.scope: Figure 3 and Figure 4 are separately fitted to the same metric plane. Only connecting nodes are shared between resolutions. Survey-level geometry is indicative where errors exceed building widths.
registration.osm_attribution: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright. Stable point controls only.

known_limits: No open scan of the archival 1893 Radionov sheet. Figure 3 resolves streets and blocks, not every lot or back lane.
Near-view building roofs and wall elevation are display approximations. Inferred houses are confined to mapped residential cells.
Outer-edge gate position accuracy is lower than in the bazaar. Some nearby garden and cemetery boundaries remain approximate.
The source limits of secondary lanes, basin depth, short unknown wall stretches and the separate Kagan town are omitted.

sources.title: Plan of Bukhara and its surroundings, instrumental survey by I. T. Poslavsky
sources.licence: Public-domain period cartography. No scan redistributed.
sources.precision: City walls, actual gates, main approaches, watercourse and cultivated fringe. Sparse interior detail.

sources.title: Description of the city of Bukhara by military engineer Captain I. T. Poslavsky
sources.licence: Public-domain period text. No transcription redistributed.
sources.precision: Period observations of covered stalls, narrow lanes, courtyard houses, walls and the distribution of pools.

sources.title: Bukhara, end of the nineteenth century, and the central Shahristan
sources.date: V. A. Lavrov 1950 Figs. 211, 295, republished by E. Giese 1980 pp. 52 and 54
sources.licence: Historical facts and measured locations consulted. No figure image, styling or text republished.
sources.precision: Regional and market-scale registrations. Street traces and use polygons only where features are visible. Fig. 3 is schematic; Fig. 4 resolves open courtyards and market ranges.

sources.title: Plan of Bukhara, Rempel redraw of the Poslavsky survey
sources.licence: Consulted for factual names and chronology. No page image redistributed.
sources.precision: Original title states 1886; redraw caption prints 1866. Read alongside the original.

sources.title: Parfenov-Fenin map account, reconstructed 1910–12 map
sources.licence: Consulted locally for corroboration. No scan or later streets redistributed.
sources.precision: Cross-checks positions and labels for source-confirmed roads and gates. The later network and railway do not enter the plan.

sources.title: UNESCO Historic Centre of Bukhara and Uzbek inscription inventory
sources.date: Historic property inscribed 1993; boundaries and monuments inventoried subsequently
sources.licence: Heritage facts and individual landmark locations consulted. No modern map reproduced.
sources.precision: Dated landmarks, property context, pools and western burial tract. GCP location only for modern references.

sources.title: E. G. Nekrasova, archival finding aid to the 1893 Radionov plan
sources.date: Describes the 1893 plan, printed p. 65 in 2003
sources.precision: Archive И-126, op. 1, kn. 1, d. 78. The page identifies the 1893 coloured plan; the original sheet was unavailable for tracing.
